learning_outcomes.text: Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

Ability to apply knowledge of occupational health and safety, prevention of occupational risks, and machine safety, according to current regulations on passive and active fire protection, and aspects of acoustic pollution.
Ability to understand and apply the basic principles of safety and prevention in engineering.
Assess the ethical consequences of decisions to be made in a specific situation, considering the impact on society and professional practice responsibility.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Demonstrate an entrepreneurial attitude in the design, development, and execution of solutions that represent a novelty or advance in the discipline.
Demonstrate initiative to organize one's own work, managing effort and time dedicated to achieving proposed objectives and goals.
Effectively apply techniques related to bibliographic search and the use of reliable data sources or other information systems.

syllabus_topics: UNIT 1.- Occupational Risk Prevention Law. Case studies.
UNIT 10.- Proper Management of Work Equipment.
teaching_methods: Participatory class: Individual or group work. Case resolution, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Laboratory: Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Seminars/Workshops: Conferences/Seminars by experts, Company visits, Attendance at fairs, Attendance at Conferences/Congresses
Tutoring: Personalized and small group attention. Instruction carried out with the aim of reviewing, reorienting class materials, learning, and completing assignments, etc.
Group work: Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects, etc. To be submitted and presented in practical classes.
Individual work: Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise development, class preparation, etc.

assessment_methods.method: Written tests. Objective tests, essay questions, short answers, conceptual maps, etc.
Problem-solving (individual) in class/Practical tests in laboratory/field/computer/classroom

assessment_rules: The evaluation is continuous. To pass, students must achieve a minimum score of 4.0 out of 10 in each evaluation instrument (I1, I2, I3) and an overall average score of 5.0 or higher. The final grade is calculated as (I1 x 0.4) + (I2 x 0.4) + (I3 x 0.2). If these requirements are not met, students must take a final exam, also needing to pass I2 to average. For the 2nd convocation, the system is the same, requiring submission of practices and the final written test, with the same grading criteria.
